text: Given client 3 and contact 133 both exist in HaloPSA, When halopsa_tickets_create is called with summary, client_id=3, tickettype_id=1, user_id=133, Then POST /Tickets is sent with user_id: 133 in its body and the tool returns the created ticket.
evidence: uv run pytest -q @ 797e97b: 127 passed, 0 failed. test_tickets_create_maps_agent_and_team extended to call halopsa_tickets_create with user_id=133 alongside halo_agent_id/team_id/category_1 and asserts sent(route) == [{..., "user_id": 133, ...}] (tests/test_handlers.py).

text: Given user_id is not passed, When halopsa_tickets_create is called with only the required fields (summary, client_id, tickettype_id), Then the posted body has no user_id key -- unchanged from today's behavior.
evidence: uv run pytest -q @ 797e97b: 127 passed. New test asserts sent(route) == [{"summary": "S", "client_id": 3, "tickettype_id": 1}] -- no user_id key -- when the call omits user_id (tests/test_handlers.py).

text: Given user_id=99999999 does not correspond to any HaloPSA contact, When halopsa_tickets_create is called with that id, Then the tool returns a not_found error naming contact 99999999, and no POST /Tickets call is made.
evidence: uv run pytest -q @ 797e97b: 127 passed. New test mocks GET /Users/99999999 -> 404, asserts out["error"]["code"] == "not_found" and "No contact 99999999" in message, and that the /Tickets POST route was never called (tests/test_records.py).

text: Given user_id, halo_agent_id, team_id and category_1 are all passed together, When halopsa_tickets_create is called, Then the posted body contains user_id, agent_id, team_id+team, and category_1 all set correctly, none overriding another.
evidence: Same run and assertion as TC1: sent(route) == [{"summary": "S", "client_id": 3, "tickettype_id": 1, "agent_id": 7, "user_id": 133, "category_1": "Hardware>Laptop", "team_id": 4, "team": "Service Desk"}] -- all four fields present together, none overriding another (tests/test_handlers.py @ 797e97b).

text: Given the live tools/list output after this change, When compared against tests/fixtures/tools_baseline.json by the existing contract-test suite, Then halopsa_tickets_create still has all of its baseline parameters, none of them became required, and no tool uses the reserved name agent_id.
evidence: uv run pytest -q @ 797e97b: both existing tests pass unmodified against the live tools/list (no fixture change needed -- user_id is additive and optional). Also manually confirmed via local smoke test: POST /mcp tools/list with placeholder headers returns 27 tools; halopsa_tickets_create's inputSchema.properties includes all baseline keys plus user_id, and required == ["summary", "client_id", "tickettype_id"] (unchanged).

text: Given a user_id was set on ticket creation (TC1), When halopsa_tickets_get is called for that ticket, Then the returned ticket's user_id still equals the id passed at creation -- confirms the contact round-trips through a read, not just the create response.
steps: With a real HaloPSA sandbox/test tenant (needs a real vendor account -- not available in this environment, per mcp-track.md 2.5 this does not block design or dev), call halopsa_users_search for a known contact and note its id
Call halopsa_tickets_create with that id as user_id, plus a valid client_id and tickettype_id
Call halopsa_tickets_get for the returned ticket id
expect: The ticket returned by halopsa_tickets_get shows user_id equal to the id passed at creation, and (if HaloPSA fills them) user_name/user_email for that same contact.
evidence: needs a real vendor account; not executed in this environment, per mcp-track.md 2.5/'completion standard' item 3 this does not block dev or INT publish. Unit coverage (TC1/TC4) proves user_id reaches the POST /Tickets body; the live round-trip through HaloPSA's own storage and halopsa_tickets_get is the one assumption flagged in the design doc's Open questions / Test strategy as not independently verified against a live tenant.
